marks.gloss_en: 'not one desirable thing (chemed) of theirs have I taken' (for Num 16:15, Steinsaltz)
'and he went and served other gods, which I did not command [anyone] to serve' (for Deut 17:3, Steinsaltz)
and they wrote for him 'the short-legged beast', and did not write for him 'the hare' (for Lev 11:6, Steinsaltz)
there is no difference between the great bamah and the small bamah except paschal offerings
ואימא גומר ומגוג? -- if the words of Japheth are admitted to the tents of Shem, say [the languages of] Gomer and Magog [are admitted]
היינו טעמא, דכתיב יפת אלהים ליפת -- the verse speaks of Japheth's beauty, not of whatever is Japheth's (= p_yofyuto_shel_yefet)
R' Chiyya bar Abba: this is the reason, as it is written 'yaft Elohim le-Yefet' -- the beauty of Japheth shall be in the tents of Shem
R' Yochanan: 'God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem' (Gen 9:27) -- the words of Japheth shall be in the tents of Shem
דתניא, רבי שמעון אומר: אף צבור לא הקריבו אלא פסחים וחובות שקבוע להם זמן -- the mishna's 'like Paschal lambs' is R' Shimon's view
whose [view is the mishna]? it is R' Shimon's
פסחים ותו לא? -- is the difference Paschal lambs and nothing more?
אימא כעין פסחים -- read: offerings like Paschal lambs (= p_kein_pesachim)
say [the mishna means]: offerings like Paschal lambs
'משיח' -- only the one anointed with oil; 'המשיח' -- to include the one of many garments [in the bull for any of the commandments]
מאי טעמיה דרבי מאיר? דתניא: ... תלמוד לומר המשיח (marker דתניא; no support kind names it)
'anointed' (Lev 4:3) -- I have only one anointed with the anointing oil
the first clause excepts only the bull for any of the commandments, so regarding the Yom Kippur bull and the tenth of the ephah the two are alike (marker: the bare הא)
it follows that regarding the Yom Kippur bull and the tenth of the ephah, this one [the anointed] and that one [of many garments] are equal

דאי רבי מאיר, הא תניא: מרובה בגדים מביא פר הבא על כל המצות -- R' Meir has the many-garments priest bring that bull, which the first clause makes the one difference (marker הא תניא; no support kind names it)
the mishna [its first clause] is not in accordance with R' Meir
אימא סיפא: the last clause excepts only the Yom Kippur bull and the tenth of the ephah, so in all their other matters the two are alike
אתאן לרבי מאיר, דתניא: שני -- כל מצות כהונה גדולה עליו, דברי רבי מאיר (marker דתניא; no support kind names it)
it follows that in all their [other] matters, this one [the serving priest] and that one [the priest who has passed] are equal
ואמר רבי יוסי: מעשה ברבי יוסף בן אלם... ואמרו: שני אינו ראוי לא לכהן גדול (a maaseh; no support kind names one)
...ולא לכהן הדיוט -- the Sages' ruling in the maaseh

a maaseh with R' Yosef ben Elem of Tzippori: a disqualification befell a high priest and they appointed him in his stead, and the matter came before the Sages (content in the gloss: its probative force is carried by the support edges)
כהן גדול -- משום איבה
כהן הדיוט -- משום מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין
the first clause is the Rabbis'
there is no difference between a priest anointed with the anointing oil and one of the many garments except the bull that comes for [transgression of] any of the commandments
there is no difference between a serving priest and a priest who has passed except the Yom Kippur bull and the tenth of the ephah
Rav Yosef: it is Rebbi, and he took it according to [different] tannaim
the only difference between Shiloh and Jerusalem is the place where offerings of lesser sanctity and second tithe are eaten
here and there, offerings of the most sacred order are eaten within the hangings
